de16_valley.topic: The tech-right turn: Andreessen manifesto, a16z endorsement and DOGE recruiting, Srinivasan's network state

claims.text: Manifesto: 'We believe in accelerationism – the conscious and deliberate propulsion of technological development ... To ensure the techno-capital upward spiral continues forever'; 'We believe any deceleration of AI will cost lives. Deaths that were preventable by the AI that was prevented from existing is a form of murder.'

Manifesto enemies: 'Our enemy is stagnation.'; 'Our enemy is statism, authoritarianism, collectivism, central planning, socialism.'; 'Our enemy is bureaucracy, vetocracy, gerontocracy, blind deference to tradition.'; 'Our enemy is corruption, regulatory capture, monopolies, cartels.'; 'Our enemy is deceleration, de-growth, depopulation'; UBI would turn people into 'zoo animals to be farmed by the state'; published 16 Oct 2023
Enemies list targets 'social responsibility', 'existential risk', 'tech ethics'; patron saints list of 56 begins with three anonymous accounts credited with founding effective accelerationism
About 5,200 words, 56 patron saints including Nietzsche, John Galt, Marinetti and Nick Land; Andreessen reworked a Marinetti line; critics Farrell, Tooze, Silver

16 July 2024: Andreessen and Horowitz explained support for Trump; Horowitz: 'the future of our business, the future of technology, and the future of America is at stake'; Andreessen called Biden's unrealized-gains tax proposal 'the final straw' and said he had voted Democratic for Clinton, Gore, Kerry, Obama, Hillary Clinton
Dec 2024: per WaPo and FT, Andreessen had no formal DOGE role but was interviewing and suggesting candidates, including from his own circle

Srinivasan defined a network state as 'a social network with a moral innovation, a sense of national consciousness, a recognised founder' plus in-person civility, a cryptocurrency and a software-encoded social contract; book out July 2022

Srinivasan: 2013 Startup School talk 'Silicon Valley's Ultimate Exit'; a16z general partner from Dec 2013; Coinbase CTO 2018-19; draws on Hirschman's exit and voice; Network School Forest City Malaysia Sept 2024; Malaysian authorities ordered operations shut July 2026; moved to Kazakhstan under a five-year MoU in 2026; considered for FDA commissioner 2017

New York Times (Cade Metz, Feb 2021) reported a 2013 email from Srinivasan to Yarvin suggesting it might be interesting to 'sic the Dark Enlightenment audience on a single vulnerable hostile reporter to dox them'; he did not respond to Insider's request for comment

de16_pipeline.topic: Documented hires and appointments from the network, 2024-26

claims.text: Announced 22 Dec 2024: Scott Kupor (a16z managing partner) to direct OPM; Sriram Krishnan (a16z general partner) senior policy advisor for AI at OSTP; Ken Howery (PayPal and Founders Fund co-founder) ambassador to Denmark; Michael Kratsios OSTP director; David Sacks (former PayPal COO) named crypto and AI czar earlier in December

Kratsios is a former chief of staff at Thiel Capital; Jim O'Neill former CEO of Thiel's foundation, picked for HHS deputy; Trae Stephens (Founders Fund) reportedly considered for deputy defense secretary; Vance worked for Thiel at Mithril; Thiel said he did not donate in 2024 because 'ending our decades-long technological and economic stagnation' was not the election's focus

O'Neill: Thiel Foundation CEO 2009-12, Mithril managing director 2012-19, Seasteading board; HHS deputy secretary confirmed 5 June 2025 (52-43), left 13 Feb 2026; acting CDC director 28 Aug 2025-13 Feb 2026; nominated NSF director 2 March 2026, confirmation not recorded

Anton: 'The Flight 93 Election' (Sept 2016, Claremont Review of Books, as Publius Decius Mus); NSC 8 Feb 2017-8 Apr 2018; then Hillsdale College Kirby Center and Claremont Institute senior fellow; Director of Policy Planning 20 Jan-15 Sep 2025; The Stakes (2020)

Signatories of the NatCon Statement of Principles include 'Peter Thiel / Founders Fund', 'Michael Anton / Hillsdale College Kirby Center' and 'Yoram Hazony / Edmund Burke Foundation (Israel)'; Vance, Yarvin and Land are not listed

Sacks announced on 26 March 2026 that he was stepping down as White House AI and crypto czar, having reached the end of his time as a special government employee (130 days per 12 months), and joining the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology as co-chair

de16_neighbours.topic: Neighbouring currents, each from its own texts

claims.text: NatCon statement (15 June 2022): 'The Bible should be read as the first among the sources of a shared Western civilization'; 'Where a Christian majority exists, public life should be rooted in Christianity'; 'accepting and living in accordance with the Constitution of 1787'; 'a strong but limited state, subject to constitutional restraints and a division of powers'; opposes 'transferring the authority of elected governments' to supranational bodies; 'uncontrolled and unassimilated immigration has become a source of weakness'; 'We condemn the use of state and private institutions to discriminate ... on the basis of race'

Thiel spoke at the opening of the first National Conservatism conference in Washington (Sunday, July 2019; organised by the Edmund Burke Foundation): called Google's conduct 'seemingly treasonous', said 'These questions need to be asked by the FBI and the CIA', called 25% China tariffs 'a floor and not a ceiling'

Vermeule: 'strong rule in the interest of attaining the common good is entirely legitimate'; 'Its main aim is certainly not to maximize individual autonomy'; bureaucracy 'not as an enemy, but as the strong hand of legitimate rule'

AP: Vance has used 'postliberal' to describe himself; at Steubenville 2022: 'You need to have a functional state that accomplishes some of the things that we care about'; praised Deneen's Regime Change at a 2023 panel; Deneen defines regime change as 'the peaceful but vigorous overthrow of a corrupt and corrupting liberal ruling class'; integralists want 'a state working in tandem with the Catholic Church'

PRRI 2024: Christian nationalism adherents 10%, sympathizers 20%, skeptics 37%, rejecters 29%; five measures incl. 'The U.S. government should declare America a Christian nation' and 'God has called Christians to exercise dominion over all areas of American society'; 38% of adherents agree 'true American patriots may need to resort to violence', 17% of all Americans

Natal Conference first held in Austin 2024; 2025 edition 28-29 March at UT's AT&T Conference Center (rented, not hosted); organiser Kevin Dolan said 'pro-natalist and the eugenic positions are ... very much aligned' (Austin Chronicle)
Vance at the March for Life, 24 Jan 2025: 'I want more babies in the United States of America'
Yudkowsky 'has strongly rejected neoreaction'; 2016 LessWrong survey 28 of 3,060 (0.92%) neoreactionary; 21.7% effective altruist; Overcoming Bias Nov 2006, LessWrong 1 Feb 2009
Thiel gave the Singularity Institute (now MIRI) $100,000 matching funds in Feb 2006 and half of $400,000 in May 2007; over $1.6 million in total per MIRI's top-contributors list

e/acc: earliest reference May 2022 by pseudonymous accounts incl. @BasedBeffJezos; Forbes identified Guillaume Verdon in Dec 2023; aims to climb the Kardashev gradient; opposes EA's AI-risk priorities; Land has expressed support; critic Thomas Murphy called it 'Nick Land diluted'; Andreessen and Garry Tan added e/acc to profiles

ISD (2022): accelerationism is 'an ideology focussed on the need for societal collapse to preserve the white race'; groups Atomwaffen, The Base, Iron March, Fascist Forge, siege culture; Mason's SIEGE; Christchurch and Poway attackers; ISD lists neoreaction ('a doctrine developed by Nick Land and Curtis Yarvin') as one of three ideological strands, noting neoreactionaries see democracy, not minorities, as the obstacle

13 Jan 2025: State designated the Terrorgram Collective and three leaders as Specially Designated Global Terrorists under EO 13224; it 'promotes violent white supremacism, solicits attacks'; Al Jazeera citing SPLC: its aim was 'accelerationism'; linked to 2022 Slovakia LGBTQ bar shooting, a planned 2024 New Jersey energy attack and an August mosque knife attack in Turkiye
